extracts.lead_summary: A third straight weekly gain, and the first close over the 50-day since mid-September — for one day. XLF rose 0.7% to $55.90 while SPY fell 0.4% and XLK was flat. Thursday's $56.65 was the best close since Sep 14 and cleared the 50D; Friday gave back 1.3% as American Express beat on adjusted EPS, missed slightly on revenue, announced a 5% job cut and fell 3.7%. The split from last week held: the money-center banks fell (C -2.9%, JPM -2.4%, BAC to its lowest close since May), while Visa, Mastercard, Berkshire and Travelers made two-year closing highs Thursday and the regionals rallied (KRE +3.8%). Customers Bancorp beat and rose 13%. October hike odds fell from about half to under 10%, the 10Y closed 5.00%, and 2s10s narrowed again to +31bp.
